title: Default language in Setup offers the languages the deployment supports, instead of four hard-coded ones
body:
epic:#26676#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_cdb7a717def74e719988f089fbaa18ff

Filed on the maintainer's word, verbatim: 「立卡」 (2026-11-05), answering their question 「如果元数据app中只有10种语言，系统管理员可以增加新的语言并且处理国际化吗？」 and the proposal below. Measured on `main` `04f36b63f8`.

## What a customer sees

A French company sets up the platform. The console has a complete French pack and a user can pick 法语 from their language menu. In Setup, 默认语言 offers only English, 简体中文, 日本語 and Español. Writing `fr-FR` is refused. So is `vi-VN`, even after the administrator has added a Vietnamese translation and the language menu offers it. Every new user in that company therefore starts in a language the company did not choose.

## Why

`packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/localization.manifest.ts:84`: the `locale` setting's options are a literal list of four, and the option list is the enforcement boundary. Three lists answer the same question differently:

| List | Contents on the test deployment |
|:--|:--|
| 默认语言 options | 4, hard-coded |
| Console's built-in packs | 10 (`ar de en es fr ja ko pt ru zh`) |
| User's language menu, `/api/v1/i18n/locales` plus what the renderer can resolve | Grows with translation items, so it gained `vi-VN` and `fr-FR` |

## Expected

- 默认语言 offers what the deployment supports, from the same source the language menu reads, and the server accepts exactly those values. Adding a translation item makes the language available here too.
- A previously saved value that is no longer offered stays readable and is shown as such, not silently replaced.
- An option's name reads in its own language, as the language menu does.

## Question for the dev to settle in the PR

Some consumers read this setting for things other than console text: the description says number and date formatting, and auth email templates read a locale too. A language with a translation item but no console pack, such as Vietnamese, then shows an English console while dates format in Vietnamese. I think that is acceptable and matches what the user menu already does, but I did not check every reader. List them in the PR, and if one breaks on a locale outside the four, stop and report.

#30206 (first-run checklist) has a row for language. It should use the list this card produces.
